newsitem.title: USA: Grandmother to face trial over parking meter flap.
newsitem.headline: Grandmother to face trial over parking meter flap.

text.p: A U.S. judge on Friday ordered a 63-year-old grandmother to stand trial for putting coins in expired parking meters after a policeman told her to stop.
"I never expected this case would drag on the way it has," Sylvia Stayton told reporters after the decision by Municipal Court Judge John West.
The jury trial was set for Feb. 5.

Stayton was arrested on Oct. 24 and charged with obstructing official business and disorderly conduct after she saw a policeman writing parking tickets and decided to drop a few coins in two meters to stop him.

She said she didn't know who the cars belonged to and only wanted to do someone a favour. The policeman who ordered her to stop arrested her and she was jailed briefly before being released on $1,900 bond.
Assistant City Prosecutor Earnest McAdams said the jury faces a difficult decision.

"You have some people who must be wondering what right she had to interfere with a policeman just doing his job, and you may have others questioning why policemen aren't out trying to catch drug dealers instead of issuing parking citations," he told reporters.
